accuracy.evidence: Ranges checked against the AQA A-level Chemistry data booklet (O–H alcohols 3230–3550, O–H acids 2500–3000, C=O 1680–1750, C–H 2850–3300, C≡N 2220–2260, C–O 1000–1300) and the OCR Chemistry A data sheet (O–H acids 2500–3300, very broad); the lesson quotes AQA in the adult text and 'about 2500–3300' for the acid in kid text and lab, noting boards differ. Trough positions of the simplified spectra checked against NIST WebBook / SDBS gas and liquid spectra: propanone C=O 1715, 1362, 1220; ethanol broad O–H ~3340, C–O ~1050; ethanoic acid C=O ~1712, C–O ~1295; propan-1-ol C–O ~1060, 970; propan-2-ol C–O ~1130, ~950, 1380/1368 isopropyl doublet, 818. Wavenumber definition (waves per cm, proportional to energy) and transmittance (absorbed = 100 − %T) verified; p4 and m7 parameter corners enumerated.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented exam slips from AQA/OCR examiner reports: reading absorptions as peaks, reading the axis as increasing left to right, calling sharp C–H near 3000 an O–H, not recognising the very broad acid O–H overlapping C–H, and trying to assign every fingerprint trough instead of matching the pattern.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is about reading a spectrum: a draggable cursor that reports wavenumber and %T and locks onto troughs, region bands placed on the real axis, spectra named by trough shape, an overlay match of propan-2-ol vs propan-1-ol in the fingerprint region, and claims judged against a trace. flagirvib (925) plucks springs to explain why bonds absorb; it has no spectrum reading, axes or fingerprint matching.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover the reversed axis and trough reading by moving the cursor and seeing the numbers fall left to right, discover that propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol overlap above 1500 but not below by overlaying them, and discover that shape separates alcohol from acid before the step text states the rule.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'rises to a peak', 'Double bonds like C=O' for the highest wavenumbers, 'narrow, at 3600' for acid O–H, and 'Yes, easily' for telling the propanols apart above 1500; each is overturned by the following task and A.reveal reports it.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge items with tagged wrong options (up, colour, dir, unit, oh, ch, ket, acid, fpoh, noise, pct), each giving a specific correction, e.g. 'At 10% transmittance, about 90% was absorbed.'

readability.evidence: Kid explanation FK grade 3.4 and adult 8.9 (limits 6.5 and 9.5) by learn/readability.py; transmittance and wavenumber are defined in plain words before use; sentences are short.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph is the axes, trough reading, regions and shapes, or the fingerprint region; adult text gives spec codes, the lab plan and named mistakes. No filler phrases; content-similarity gate passes against all lessons including 925.

mobile.evidence: Canvas uses a taller ratio under 520 px; the whole plot is the cursor's drag target; region bands carry short tags (X–H, ≡, C=O, fingerprint) so labels fit at 390 px; reference chips and every action have full-size buttons. Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots.

accessibility.evidence: Cursor moves with ±100 and ±10 cm⁻¹ buttons, regions and references have buttons, naming and claims are buttons; the canvas aria-label lists the current spectrum's trough positions, cursor value and progress; axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and phone (walk.cjs).
